#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script converted from PBS
# Note: Flux does not support in-script directives for resource specification
# This script should be submitted with the following command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 24 -t 1h --job-name=array_job --output=/mnt/lustre/users/blombard/reinfectionsBelinda/oe_files/array_job_m1-{{id}}.out --error=/mnt/lustre/users/blombard/reinfectionsBelinda/oe_files/array_job_m1-{{id}}.err script.sh
#
# For array job functionality, submit with:
# flux batch --array=1-21:21 -N 1 -n 24 -t 1h --job-name=array_job --output=/mnt/lustre/users/blombard/reinfectionsBelinda/oe_files/array_job_m1-{{id}}.out --error=/mnt/lustre/users/blombard/reinfectionsBelinda/oe_files/array_job_m1-{{id}}.err script.sh
#
# Resource specifications:
# -N 1         : 1 node (from select=1)
# -n 24        : 24 tasks (from ncpus=24)
# -t 1h        : 1 hour walltime (from walltime=1:00:00)
# --job-name=array_job : job name (from -N array_job)
# --output=/mnt/lustre/users/blombard/reinfectionsBelinda/oe_files/array_job_m1-{{id}}.out : stdout file
# --error=/mnt/lustre/users/blombard/reinfectionsBelinda/oe_files/array_job_m1-{{id}}.err : stderr file
# --array=1-21:21 : array job indices 1-21 with stride 21 (from -J 1-21:21)
#
# Note: Flux uses {{id}} for job ID instead of PBS's automatic numbering
# Note: PBS -J creates array jobs; Flux uses --array flag

# Original PBS project: CBBI1106
# PBS: -P CBBI1106
# Note: Flux uses banks/accounts through flux-accounting
# Set at submission if flux-accounting is configured:
# flux batch --setattr=bank=CBBI1106 ...
# Performance impact: Without project/account specification, job may run under default account
# which could affect priority, resource limits, or accounting tracking

# Original PBS queue: smp
# PBS: -q smp
# Note: Flux does not have queues in the same way as PBS
# Queue selection is handled through Flux's scheduling configuration
# Performance impact: Job scheduling priority depends on site-specific Flux configuration
# Consult site documentation for equivalent resource pools or queues

# Original PBS email: belindalombard@sun.ac.za with notifications for begin and end
# PBS: -M belindalombard@sun.ac.za -m be
# Note: Flux does not have built-in email notification directives
# Performance impact: User must manually monitor job status or implement external
# monitoring solutions using flux job events, flux watch commands, or wrapper scripts
# Consider creating notification wrappers or using flux job attach with monitoring

# Original PBS array job: -J 1-21:21
# PBS array indices: 1-21 with stride of 21 (only indices 1 and 22, but 22 > 21, so effectively just index 1)
# Flux: --array=1-21:21 at submission
# Note: PBS_ARRAY_INDEX becomes FLUX_TASK_ID in Flux
# The array specification 1-21:21 with stride 21 means only task ID 1 will run
# (starting at 1, incrementing by 21, but 22 exceeds the maximum of 21)

sleep 4

# Module loading
#module add chpc/BIOMODULES R/4.1.0
module add chpc/R/3.5.1-gcc7.2.0

# Change to working directory
cd /mnt/lustre/users/blombard/reinfectionsBelinda/

# Execute make command
make sbv

# Array job logic
STEP=21

# PBS uses PBS_ARRAY_INDEX; Flux uses FLUX_TASK_ID
# If not running as array job, default to 1
START=${FLUX_TASK_ID:-1}
END=$(( $START+$STEP-1 ))

for i in $(eval echo "{$START..$END}")
do
	(echo "process $i started" && Rscript sbv/method_1_analysis/method_1_arrayjob.R $i && echo "process $i finished")& 
done

sleep 0.1 # For sequential output
echo "Waiting for processes to finish" 
wait $(jobs -p)
echo "All processes finished"

# Note on array jobs:
# Flux array jobs use FLUX_TASK_ID instead of PBS_ARRAY_INDEX
# The original PBS script had -J 1-21:21, which creates array with indices: 1
# (stride of 21 means: start at 1, next would be 1+21=22, but that exceeds max of 21)
# If the intent was to create 21 separate array tasks, use: --array=1-21 (no stride)
# If the intent was to process items 1-21 in a single job, the current script is correct

# Complete submission command for single job:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 24 -t 1h \
#   --job-name=array_job \
#   --output=/mnt/lustre/users/blombard/reinfectionsBelinda/oe_files/array_job_m1-{{id}}.out \
#   --error=/mnt/lustre/users/blombard/reinfectionsBelinda/oe_files/array_job_m1-{{id}}.err \
#   --setattr=bank=CBBI1106 \
#   script.sh
#
# Complete submission command for array job (if intent was 21 separate jobs):
# flux batch --array=1-21 -N 1 -n 24 -t 1h \
#   --job-name=array_job \
#   --output=/mnt/lustre/users/blombard/reinfectionsBelinda/oe_files/array_job_m1-{{id}}.out \
#   --error=/mnt/lustre/users/blombard/reinfectionsBelinda/oe_files/array_job_m1-{{id}}.err \
#   --setattr=bank=CBBI1106 \
#   script.sh

issues: The script correctly documents resource specifications and properly converts PBS directives to Flux command-line options.
Resource allocation is appropriate: 1 node, 24 tasks, 1 hour walltime.

The array job specification '--array=1-21:21' with stride 21 will only create one array task (index 1), not 21 tasks as might be intended. The documentation correctly notes this behavior. If the intent was to create 21 separate array jobs, the submission should use '--array=1-21' without the stride.

The script logic processes indices 1-21 sequentially within a single job by spawning background processes, which is functional but may not be the most efficient use of resources. With 24 allocated tasks (-n 24) but spawning only 21 background R processes, 3 tasks are unused.

The background process spawning (using '&') within the for loop will attempt to run 21 R processes concurrently. With only 24 cores allocated, this could lead to resource contention if each R process uses multiple threads. Consider if this parallelization strategy aligns with the resource allocation.

No memory specification is provided. The original PBS script also lacked explicit memory constraints, but for 21 concurrent R processes, explicit memory allocation might be beneficial to prevent out-of-memory errors.
The output file pattern uses '{{id}}' which is correct for Flux job ID substitution. However, for array jobs, consider using '{{id}}.{{taskid}}' to distinguish between array task outputs.
The script uses FLUX_TASK_ID with a default of 1 if not set. This is appropriate for handling both array and non-array job submissions.

The 'make sbv' command is executed before the parallel processing, which could be a bottleneck if it's time-consuming and should ideally complete within the 1-hour walltime along with the R processing.
No validation that the working directory or required files exist before attempting to execute make or Rscript commands.
